identity.name: Lan Na
alt_names: Chiang Mai (Lan Na under Burmese rule)

land.text: the same 180 cells after Mekuti's capture in November 1564

predecessors.note: The same state, not a new one: Cliopatria's 'Lan Na Kingdom' (1294-1563) and 'Lan Na' (1600-1761) rows share Wikidata Q1059707 and the Lan Na article, whose infobox runs 'Capital: Chiang Mai (1296-1775)'. The lan-na-kingdom dossier (another batch) stops in November 1564 and names this slug as successor; the colour continues. Merging the two into the earlier slug is the orchestrator's call (see notes).

land.text: the Chiang Mai principality, the same land, under Siamese suzerainty

successors.note: Kawila of Lampang 'captured the city on 15 January 1775'; Kawila became prince of Lampang and Phraya Chaban (the page's spelling) prince of Chiang Mai, 'both Siamese vassals' (Lan Na page). The Kingdom of Chiang Mai is another batch's state; the suzerain, the Thonburi Kingdom, carries the vassal event.

capitals.name: Chiang Mai
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Chiang Mai (1296-1775)'. Occupied by the Siamese for part of 1663 (Burmese-Siamese War page).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1600 outline (52,632 km2, 179 cells) for 1565-1599: the same land under Burmese suzerainty

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1565-1599 on Cliopatria's 1600 outline: Lan Na is a Burmese tributary ('Tributary of Burma (1st): 1558-1596'); 'the king was captured by Burmese forces in November 1564' and Bayinnaung made the Lan Na royal Wisutthithewi queen regnant (no dates); Nawrahta Minsaw was appointed viceroy 'in January 1579'. The page gives no territory; the 180 cells of the Lan Na Kingdom shape of 1563 hold (the 1600 outline has 179 of them). No area on the page, so no infobox check.

1600-1618: 52,632 km2 (179 cells). 'Lan Na's Nawrahta Minsaw declared independence in 1596' and became 'a vassal of Naresuan' in 1602 (infobox 'Tributary of Ayutthaya: 1596-1615'); Siam's control was 'at most nominal' by 1614 and when the Burmese returned in 1614-1615 Thado Kyaw sought help from Lan Xang. The land does not change; the page names no territory and gives no area.

correction.text: the 1600 outline for 1619-1733: Lan Na as a Burmese tributary state (the tint belongs to the suzerain's ledger)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1619-1733 on the 1600 outline, where Cliopatria has no shape: 'Tributary of Burma (2nd): 1615-1628', 'Independent state: 1628-1631', 'Tributary of Burma (3rd): 1631-1727', and, after 1614, vassal kings of Burmese descent ruled Lan Na for over a century (page, paraphrased). Siam took Chiang Mai in February 1663 and left that year (Burmese-Siamese War page). In 1727 Chiang Mai revolted and 'Chiang Mai and Ping valley became independent' after 1731-32; the page clearly places only Chiang Mai and the Ping valley under Lan Na after 1727, so the land after 1727 may be smaller than the 180 cells.

1734-1737: 52,465 km2 (179 cells), the 1600 outline within a cell; Chiang Mai and the Ping valley independent after the revolt of 1727-1732 (infobox 'Independent city-states: 1727-1763'). Ong Kham of Luang Prabang, 'offered the throne of Lanna in 1727', ruled to 1769 (Ong Kham page).
1738-1740: 52,438 km2, within a cell of 1734; no event on the page.
1741-1756: 52,798 km2, within a cell; no event on the page. Konbaung rises in Burma in these years (neighbour list).

correction.text: shape unchanged; Burmese tributary status from 1757 (text) or 1763 (infobox), carried by the suzerain's vassal events

keyframe_review.note: 1757-1761: 52,798 km2, unchanged. Status only: Chiang Mai 'became a vassal again' to the Konbaung dynasty in 1757 (text; the infobox has 'Independent city-states: 1727-1763' and 'Tributary of Burma (4th): 1763-1774'). The land does not change.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1757 outline for 1762-1775, to the Siamese conquest of 15 January 1775

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1762-1775, where Cliopatria's row has ended (1761): a revolt of 1761-1763 with Siamese encouragement was suppressed by January 1763; Burma used Lan Na as a base against Laos and Siam from 1765; Kawila of Lampang took Chiang Mai on 15 January 1775 with Siamese help.

region.text: the Chiang Mai and Ping valley land of the Lan Na kingdom, the same 180 cells

ledger.note: 1565: Lan Na goes on under Burmese rule. 'The king was captured by Burmese forces in November 1564' and sent to Pegu; Bayinnaung made the Lan Na royal Wisutthithewi 'the queen regnant of Lan Na' (no date). No new state: the lan-na-kingdom dossier hands over its 180 cells and its colour.

January 1579: a Burmese prince governs Lan Na. Nawrahta Minsaw was appointed viceroy 'in January 1579'; Burma allowed substantial autonomy but strictly controlled corvée and taxation (page, paraphrased). Same state and colour; the ruling line changes from the Mangrai kings to Burmese viceroys.

region.text: Lan Na, which the Siamese invaded and from which they later 'relinquished control'

ledger.note: February 1663: Narai takes Chiang Mai. 'King Narai and two Siamese armies invaded Lan Na and captured Chiang Mai in February 1663' (the march began in December 1662); 'When the Burmese army did arrive they were caught in a trap, routed, and forced to return to Ava.' Hatched, not annexed. The month is left out so that the end, which has none, can follow it in order.

Later in 1664: the Siamese leave. 'Later that year, the Siamese relinquished control of Lan Na and returned to Siam as a result of a rebellious populace'; the page gives no year; the nearest dated event before it is the Siamese retreat of May 1664, so 1664 (reviewer se-01-h; ayutthaya-kingdom has 1663).

1727: Chiang Mai revolts and a new ruling line takes the throne. 'In 1727, Chiang Mai revolted because of high taxation'; 'Ong Kham was offered the throne of Lanna in 1727' and 'ruled until his death in 1769' (Ong Kham page) while the Lan Na page has a Lao king, Ong Kham of Luang Prabang, dominate Chiang Mai 'for more than 30 years'. The page's infobox last ruler Po Mayu-nguan (1768-1775) conflicts with the Ong Kham page's dates. Same state and colour; the suzerain's ledger ends the Burmese tributary tint in 1727.

region.text: the Chiang Mai principality, now a Siamese vassal

ledger.note: 15 January 1775: Chiang Mai falls to the Siamese. Kawila of Lampang revolted with Siamese help and 'captured the city on 15 January 1775'; infobox 'Siamese conquest: 15 January 1775'. The Burmese governor Thado Mindin was unpopular.

wars.name: Burmese–Siamese War (1662–1664)
wars.outcome: Burmese defensive victory: Narai took Chiang Mai in February 1663 and left later that year because of a rebellious populace; Lan Na stayed within the Burmese orbit.
wars.note: The Lan Na page says only that Siam tried to take Lan Na but failed in 1662-1664; the war page has the capture in February 1663.

wars.name: Chiang Mai revolt against Burma (1727–1732)
wars.outcome: Lan Na victory: the resistance drove back Burmese armies in 1727-1728 and 1731-1732, after which 'Chiang Mai and Ping valley became independent'.

wars.name: Lan Na revolt of 1761–1763
wars.outcome: Burmese victory: a revolt with Siamese encouragement was suppressed by January 1763; the infobox has Lan Na a Burmese tributary again from 1763 to 1774.

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Lan Na
wars.outcome: Siamese victory: Kawila of Lampang revolted with Siamese help and captured Chiang Mai on 15 January 1775; Kawila became prince of Lampang and Phraya Chaban prince of Chiang Mai, both Siamese vassals.
wars.note: The Lan Na page links Burmese-Siamese War (1775-1776) and 'Siamese conquest of Lan Na (1775)', not opened.

certainty.note: No page gives Lan Na's extent in these years; Cliopatria's outline of Chiang Mai, Lamphun, Lampang and the Ping valley is approximate throughout.

sources.title: Lan Na
sources.note: Identity, infobox suzerainty spans 1558-1775, Mekuti 1564, 1579 viceroy, 1596 independence, 1727 revolt, 1757, 1761-63, 15 January 1775. No area, no territory.

sources.title: Burmese–Siamese War (1662–1664)
sources.note: The Siamese capture of Chiang Mai in February 1663 and withdrawal later that year.

sources.title: Ong Kham
sources.note: Offered the throne of Lanna in 1727, ruled to 1769; page does not describe Chiang Mai's governance or territory.

notes:
One state, two Cliopatria rows: 'Lan Na Kingdom' (1294-1563, lan-na-kingdom dossier of another batch, ends November 1564) and 'Lan Na' (1600-1761) share Wikidata Q1059707 and the Lan Na article. This dossier continues the same land and colour from 1565 to the Siamese conquest of 15 January 1775 and fills the periods where Cliopatria has no shape (1565-1599, 1619-1733, 1762-1775) with the 180-cell outline (1600 and 1734 differ from the 1563 shape by one cell). The brief asks for one dossier under the earlier slug with both Names; lan-na-kingdom is another batch's file and was not edited. To merge, add 'Lan Na' to lan-na-kingdom's cliopatria_names, move this dossier's keyframes and ledger into it, and drop the 1564 dissolve there.
Vassalage is the suzerain's record, not drawn here: first-toungoo-empire carries Burma's tributary spans (1564, 1596, 1614, 1628, 1631, 1727 in its ledger) and ayutthaya-kingdom its 1600-1618 span; still needed from other batches: konbaung-dynasty 'vassal_start lan-na' in 1757 (page text) or 1763 (infobox) and thonburi-kingdom 'vassal_start chiangmai' in 1775; chiangmai must start in January 1775 on the same land.
Page conflicts: Ayutthaya as suzerain 1596-1615 (infobox), 1602 (text), 1600 (ayutthaya ledger); 'Independent city-states 1727-1763' (infobox) against 'became a vassal again in 1757' (text); who ruled after 1727 (Ong Kham of Luang Prabang 1727-1769 on his page against the infobox's last ruler Po Mayu-nguan 1768-1775); the Lan Na page says Siam tried to take Lan Na but failed in 1662-64 while the war page has Chiang Mai captured in February 1663.
Not on the pages: any extent for Lan Na between 1558 and 1775 (Nan, Phrae, Lampang, Lamphun, Chiang Saen, the Shan states appear only in earlier or later contexts), so no gain or loss is dated and the area check was impossible; Mae Hong Son and the Shan states of Laihka, Hsipaw, Mong Nai and Yawnghwe, undated expansion in the lan-na-kingdom notes, are not in this dossier. The Cliopatria row ends in 1761 although the state lasted to 1775. Page budget 3 of 5.
